correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the normalized finite-abelian-group STFT with counting measure, row products h_x=f(y)conj(g(y−x)), r_x=|supp h_x|, n_x=|supp Fourier(h_x)|. Parseval and Cauchy–Schwarz prove r_x n_x≥N; overlap sum ∑r_x=ab, k=|supp f−supp g|≥max(a,b), hence total M=∑n_x≥Nk²/(ab)≥N. Unequal a,b force M>N+1. Equal support sizes m<N: k≥m+1 gives M>N+1; k=m forces both supports to be cosets of a common subgroup H of size m; all Fourier rows have support divisible by N/m≥2, contradicting M=N+1. Full supports a=b=N: N−1 one-frequency rows imply, for each group shift d, all translate-ratios of g are scalar characters, so the remaining row also has one frequency and M=N. For N=2 the explicit support-three counterexample explains the exact N≥3 boundary. Proof is symbolic and covers all finite abelian groups without prime or full-support assumptions.

originality.rationale: Qualified PASS: the support-minimum inequality M≥N, subgroup extremizer framework, and prime cyclic support-gap strengthening are previously established. The surviving claim is the universal exclusion of precisely N+1 for all finite abelian groups N≥3, including composite/noncyclic groups not implied by the odd-prime cyclic p-or-≥2p theorem; neither the retrieved general uncertainty statements nor cyclic equality cases state this general one-step gap.
residual_risks: The odd-prime cyclic subcase is already dominated by a stronger published theorem; novelty is only the universal composite/noncyclic extension.
Unindexed finite-Gabor support spectra or stronger full-text general uncertainty statements may contain an equivalent exclusion.
The N+2 cardinality is not proved attainable or optimal.

value.rationale: PASS: the natural next cardinality above the sharp global STFT uncertainty minimum is excluded uniformly for an entire class of finite groups. It is a structural forbidden-support statement distinct from a routine restatement of the minimum bound, with a sharp restriction N≥3 and legitimate applications to Gabor support spectra. It does not assert that N+2 is attained or the optimal second support level.
